glossary.Tricuspid valve: The three-leaflet valve between the right atrium and right ventricle.
glossary.Pulmonary valve: The valve between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery to the lungs.
glossary.RA: Right atrium, the chamber receiving blood from the body.
glossary.RV: Right ventricle, the chamber that pumps blood to the lungs.
glossary.Congenital heart disease: A heart abnormality present from birth.
glossary.Rheumatic disease: Heart valve damage after rheumatic fever, an immune reaction to strep throat.
glossary.Regurgitation: Backward leak of blood through a valve that does not close properly.
glossary.Systole: The phase of the heartbeat when the ventricles contract.
glossary.Diastole: The phase of the heartbeat when the ventricles relax and fill.
glossary.Lower left sternal edge: The area just left of the lower breastbone, where tricuspid murmurs are best heard.
glossary.Left upper sternal border: The area just left of the upper breastbone (pulmonary area).
glossary.Pulmonary area: The second left intercostal space beside the sternum, where pulmonary valve sounds are best heard.
glossary.Left heart failure: The left ventricle cannot pump well, so pressure backs up into the lungs.
glossary.Exertional syncope: Fainting during physical effort, because the heart cannot raise its output.
glossary.Peripheral oedema: Swelling of the legs and ankles from fluid build-up.
glossary.Staphylococcus aureus: A common skin bacterium and the usual cause of endocarditis in people who inject drugs.
glossary.Staph aureus: Short for Staphylococcus aureus, a skin bacterium that commonly causes endocarditis.
glossary.IV drug use: Injecting drugs into a vein, which carries skin bacteria straight to the right heart.
glossary.Aortic stenosis: Narrowing of the aortic valve, giving an ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids.
glossary.Carotids: The main arteries in the neck supplying the head and brain.
glossary.Pulmonary emboli: Clots or infected debris that lodge in the arteries of the lungs.
glossary.ECG: Electrocardiogram: a recording of the heart's electrical activity.
glossary.Diuretics: Drugs that make the kidneys remove more salt and water.
glossary.Fluid overload: Too much fluid in the body, causing swelling and breathlessness.
glossary.Valve replacement: Surgery that swaps a diseased valve for a mechanical or tissue valve.
glossary.Valve repair: Surgery that fixes the patient's own valve rather than replacing it.
glossary.Intrathoracic pressure: The pressure inside the chest cavity, which falls when you breathe in.
glossary.Venous return: The flow of blood back to the heart through the veins.
glossary.Hepatic congestion: Blood backing up in the liver because of high venous pressure.
glossary.Septic emboli: Infected clumps of clot and bacteria that break off a valve and lodge elsewhere.
glossary.Outflow obstruction: A blockage to blood leaving a ventricle.
glossary.Palpable thrill: A vibration felt with the hand over a loud murmur.
glossary.Pressure gradient: The difference in pressure across a narrowed valve, measured on echo to grade severity.
